title: Admissions benchmark item
description: One verified question-answer pair about university admissions. Every field is either recorded from an official source or assigned by the sampling design. This file is the human-readable contract; src/validate.py enforces it.

id.description: Stable slug, lowercase-hyphenated. Convention: <university>-<program>-<fact>-<qualifier>. Never reused, never renumbered.

university.description: Institution name exactly as it appears on its own official site.

coverage_tier.description: How well represented the institution is in the English-language web. Assigned per institution in docs/universities.md, never per item, so the axis stays consistent.

question_en.description: The question in English. Must name the institution, the program level, and the admissions cycle explicitly, so the answer is unambiguous without context.

question_ru.description: The same question in Russian. A translation of question_en, not a separate question: any difference in what is asked confounds the language axis.

fact_type.description: What kind of fact is being asked about.

volatility.description: annual = the correct answer changes every admissions cycle. stable = it does not change year to year.

gold_answer.description: The correct answer in canonical form, as stated by the official source on date_accessed.

acceptable_variants.description: Other surface forms of the same answer that must be scored correct: alternative date formats, currency notation, the Russian rendering. Not a place for approximately-correct answers.

prior_year_answer.description: The value this same fact held in the previous admissions cycle, or null for stable facts and for facts with no documented prior value. This is what makes the stale-versus-fabricated error split possible: an incorrect answer matching this string means the model is out of date rather than inventing. See docs/design_decisions.md DD-003.

source_url.description: The official university page the answer was read from. Not a ranking site, not an aggregator, not Wikipedia.

source_quote.description: The exact sentence from the source that establishes the answer. Copied verbatim. This is what a reader checks the claim against.

snapshot_path.description: Repo-relative path to the archived copy of source_url. The page will change; the snapshot is the evidence.

date_accessed.description: ISO date the source was read. Reported in the paper: these numbers are a photograph of a moment.

verification_round.description: 1 after the first pass, 2 after the independent second pass. Only round-2 items go in the final dataset.

round1_gold_answer.description: What the first pass recorded, filled in during the second pass only when the two passes disagreed. The count of non-null values here is the inter-pass disagreement rate reported in the paper. Do not overwrite the round-1 value to make it match.

notes.description: Anything a reader needs to interpret this item: source pages contradicting each other, ambiguous wording, a fact that turned out to be conditional. May be empty. A source contradicting itself is a finding, not a data problem.
